comments.body:
PRE-REVIEW VERIFICATION against the code S1/S2/S4 actually landed on the stack (front-loaded because three plans in this epic have already had a wrong claim about a SIBLING story, and each cost a review cycle).

TWO SCOPE ITEMS ARE ALREADY DONE — this plan overstates its own work:

(1) 'Bedrock-hosted Claude gets a rebar ModelProfile override because its capability flags differ from the direct Anthropic API' — ALREADY SHIPPED by f184 (closed). src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:38 _is_claude() covers BOTH hosts: isinstance(profile, AnthropicModelProfile) OR bedrock_thinking_variant == 'anthropic', and the _REBAR_OVERRIDES entry withdraws native_structured_output for both. f184 also added the boto3-gated verified-fake test pinning that Bedrock Claude's real profile carries those fields. S3 must NOT re-add this; it should verify it and move on.

(2) 'Prompt caching is wired through BedrockModelSettings ... selected by the prompt_cache_style == "bedrock" capability' — the SELECTION is already shipped: capabilities.py:198 cache_settings_for() returns BedrockModelSettings when prompt_cache_style == 'bedrock', and f184 carries a boto3-gated test asserting both cache keys are set. S3 supplies the missing half only: the builder that makes a Bedrock model exist so that branch is reachable in production.

ONE GENUINE CONTRADICTION TO RESOLVE BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION — the number of cache keys:

This plan names THREE (bedrock_cache_instructions, bedrock_cache_tool_definitions, bedrock_cache_messages). f184 shipped TWO (instructions + tool_definitions) and DELIBERATELY omitted messages, because the direct-Anthropic path sets exactly anthropic_cache_instructions + anthropic_cache_tool_definitions and PARITY was the goal — AnthropicModelSettings also has anthropic_cache_messages and rebar does not set it either.

So enabling bedrock_cache_messages would make Bedrock cache MORE than the Anthropic path, which is not parity but a new caching behaviour with its own cost/TTL profile. Recommendation: keep TWO keys for parity, and if message-level caching is wanted, make it a separate decision with its own measurement rather than smuggling it in as a third key here. Whichever is chosen, this plan and f184's shipped code must AGREE — right now they do not, and the S6 parity bar is measured against exactly this.

ALSO CONFIRMED CORRECT in this plan: the [bedrock] extra is genuinely still absent (f184 carries an AC that it added no boto3 dependency), and pydantic_ai.models.bedrock does import botocore at module top, so the missing-extra error path is real. The unit-tests-without-AWS-credentials AC is achievable — capabilities.py already imports BedrockModelSettings INSIDE the bedrock branch precisely so no botocore import happens unless a Bedrock model is in use.

STALE CITATION WARNING: this plan cites no line numbers, which is good, but note runner.py is now at EXACTLY the 800-LOC hard cap (task 2682) and providers.py is at 289 against the 300-LOC cap that is an ATTESTED criterion of closed story 7468. The bedrock builder will NOT fit in providers.py. It needs its own leaf module (e.g. src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py, mirroring anthropic_model.py) — decide that in the plan rather than leaving the implementer to breach a signed criterion.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
MEASURED BEDROCK FINDINGS — real AWS calls, account 5797...98, profile frontier, region us-east-2, via boto3 Converse and pydantic-ai BedrockConverseModel. Oracle: same request twice with a cachePoint after a ~4000-token stable system prefix; read cacheReadInputTokens/cacheWriteInputTokens off the real response (no latency inference).

1) ON-DEMAND MODEL IDS ARE NOT INVOKABLE HERE AT ALL. Both anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 and the old anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0 return ValidationException: 'Invocation of model ID ... with on-demand throughput isnt supported. Retry your request with the ID or ARN of an inference profile.' So this storys framing — compare a plain on-demand id against an inference-profile ARN and pick — is moot in this environment: only inference profiles work. rebars documented default MUST be an inference-profile id.

2) PROMPT CACHING WORKS WITH A REGIONAL INFERENCE PROFILE. us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6: attempt 1 cache_write=4017 cache_read=0; attempt 2 cache_write=0 cache_read=4017. Reproducible — a later run hit a still-warm cache (cache_read=4017 on attempt 1, 5-min TTL). This REFUTES the premise of pydantic-ai #4381 (that a cross-region inference profile silently breaks caching) for this model/region.

3) CACHING IS MODEL-DEPENDENT AND FAILS SILENTLY. us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0 AND global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0 both returned cache_read=0 AND cache_write=0 on both attempts, with the full 4029 input tokens billed every call — no error, no warning. CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST INFERENCE: I initially attributed this to the global. prefix; a controlled same-model comparison (us. vs global. for opus-4-5) showed BOTH fail, so the discriminator is the MODEL, not the profile prefix. This silent double-billing is the real hazard #4381 is circling.

4) Haiku 3 + cachePoint hard-fails: us.anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0 -> AccessDeniedException You invoked an unsupported model or your request did not allow prompt caching.

5) NEW, HIGH SEVERITY, NOT IN THIS PLAN — TEMPERATURE IS FATAL ON BEDROCK FOR SOME MODELS. us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 with temperature=0 -> ValidationException/400 temperature is deprecated for this model; the identical call WITHOUT temperature succeeds. Confirmed through pydantic-ai too: BedrockConverseModel + BedrockModelSettings(temperature=0.0) -> ModelHTTPError status_code 400; without temperature -> OK.

Why this breaks rebar on Bedrock: runner.py sets model_settings[temperature] whenever cfg.temperature or req.config.temperature is set, and the plan-review Pass-2 verify steps deliberately send temperature=0 (greedy, so re-verifying a finding does not resample). pydantic-ais _drop_unsupported_sampling_settings exists ONLY in models/anthropic.py — NOT in models/bedrock.py (grepped) — so the direct-Anthropic path is protected (it warns Sampling parameters [temperature] are not supported ... will be ignored) and the Bedrock path is NOT. A Bedrock gate run on such a model therefore hard-fails rather than degrading.

CONSEQUENCES THIS PLAN MUST ABSORB BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION:
- default/documented model id must be an inference profile, and us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 is the VERIFIED caching default;
- caching must be measured per model, and because failure is silent, rebar should WARN when caching was requested but cache_read and cache_write are both 0 (an analogue of the existing _warn_if_zeroed_usage), otherwise operators silently pay full input on every call;
- the Bedrock builder must not send an unsupported sampling parameter. This needs a real decision (omit temperature on Bedrock, gate it on a capability, or pin supported models) — it cannot be left to the implementer, and it directly threatens story eb6e (S8, production review-bot cutover with no Anthropic fallback).

Raw probe scripts: /Users/joeoakhart/.claude/jobs/4ca991d2/tmp/bedrock_cache_probe.py (+probe2/3/4 variants).

WHERE I MEASURED: account 5797...98, region us-east-2, IAM user joe_sec (profile "frontier"), which holds AmazonBedrockFullAccess (bedrock:*).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
NOTE ON A LOCAL EXIT-1 THAT IS NOT A CODE DEFECT — recorded because "7542 passed, exit 1" would otherwise look like a hidden failure.

The final local full-suite run reported: 7542 passed, 29 skipped, 115 deselected, 0 failed, 0 errors — and exit code 1.

Cause: tests/conftest.py's pytest_sessionfinish REPO-ISOLATION guard. It snapshots `git status --porcelain` at session start, compares at finish, and escalates a clean run to TESTS_FAILED if the working tree gained entries — deliberately without emitting a FAILED line, so CI catches a test that wrote into the checkout instead of tmp_path.

It fired on MY contamination, not on the code: while that suite was running I edited infra/terraform/iam.tf and ran terraform init/apply in the SAME worktree for story 9249. `infra/terraform/iam.tf` was therefore newly-modified between snapshot and finish. (.terraform/ itself is gitignored, so the sole leaked entry was the .tf edit.)

Why this does not weaken this ticket's "full gating suite passes" criterion: that criterion is discharged by GERRIT CHANGE 1043's **Verified +1**, which is CI running the same gates on a FRESH checkout with no concurrent mutation — strictly better evidence than a local run. The local run's test result (7542 passed / 0 failed) is itself unaffected; only the session exit code was escalated.

LESSON, and it is mine: do not mutate the working tree while a gating suite is running in it. The guard is correct and I tripped it. Future infra work in this epic should happen in a separate checkout, or be sequenced after the suite completes.

compiled_state.description:
# S3 — First-class AWS Bedrock provider (native, no gateway) with measured prompt caching

## Context / Problem

rebar has no Bedrock path. Our clients will reach Claude through Bedrock more often than through the direct
Anthropic API, and PR #121's answer — front Bedrock with an OpenAI-compatible gateway — forces every operator
to stand up and accredit a proxy, and gives up prompt caching, the retrying transport, and native structured
output in the process.

## Approach

Register a `bedrock` builder in the provider factory [rebar:7468-25e5-ae4f-43d1] that constructs pydantic-ai's
native `BedrockConverseModel` with a `BedrockProvider`, authenticating through the ambient AWS credential chain
(instance role in production, `AWS_PROFILE`/env locally) — no rebar-managed key. Prompt caching is already selected by the
`prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"` capability shipped in story f184, which sets **exactly two** keys —
`bedrock_cache_instructions` and `bedrock_cache_tool_definitions`. An earlier draft of this plan named a third
(`bedrock_cache_messages`); that is **rejected** for parity, because the direct-Anthropic path sets only the
matching two and `AnthropicModelSettings.anthropic_cache_messages` is likewise left unset. Enabling message
caching on Bedrock alone would make it cache MORE than Anthropic, which is a new behaviour with its own cost
and TTL profile — a separate decision with its own measurement, not a third key smuggled in here. The parity
bar in story 0d76 is measured against exactly these two keys. Ships as a new `[bedrock]` optional extra
(`pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]`) so boto3 stays out of the default `[agents]` install; the builder raises a clear
missing-extra error, mirroring `runner._import_pydantic_ai`.

**Caching HAS been measured (real AWS, us-east-2, account 5797…98).** The measurement is done; this section
records the results and the decisions they force, so no implementer has to guess. Oracle: the same request twice
with a `cachePoint` after a ~4000-token stable system prefix, reading `cacheReadInputTokens` /
`cacheWriteInputTokens` off the real Converse response.

1. **On-demand model ids are not invokable at all** in this account/region — both
   `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` and the older `anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0` return
   `ValidationException: Invocation of model ID … with on-demand throughput isn't supported. Retry your request
   with the ID or ARN of an inference profile.` So this story's original on-demand-vs-profile comparison is
   moot: **only inference profiles work**, and rebar's documented default must be one.
2. **A regional inference profile DOES cache.** `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`: attempt 1
   `cache_write=4017, cache_read=0`; attempt 2 `cache_write=0, cache_read=4017`; reproducible across runs (a
   later run hit a still-warm cache, 5-minute TTL). This **refutes the premise of pydantic-ai #4381** for this
   model/region — the issue this story was built around does not reproduce.
3. **Caching is MODEL-dependent and fails SILENTLY.** `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0` and
   `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0` both report `cache_read=0` AND `cache_write=0` on both
   attempts, billing the full 4029 input tokens every call — no error, no warning. A controlled same-model
   comparison (`us.` vs `global.`) showed BOTH fail, so the discriminator is the **model**, not the profile
   prefix. Silent full-price billing is the real hazard here.
4. `us.anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0` with a `cachePoint` hard-fails:
   `AccessDeniedException: You invoked an unsupported model or your request did not allow prompt caching.`

**Decision A — the default is `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`**, the verified-caching regional inference
profile. Config accepts any profile id; this is what the docs recommend and what the parity story measures.

**Decision B — rebar must WARN when caching was requested but both counters are zero.** Because failure is
silent, an operator otherwise pays full input price on every call forever with no signal.

**It cannot reuse `_warn_if_zeroed_usage`, and that is the whole point of specifying it.** That guard fires on
`requests > 0 AND input_tokens == 0 AND output_tokens == 0` — the zeroed-adapter case. The measured Bedrock
failure is the opposite shape: `input_tokens=4029` (a perfectly healthy count) with `cache_read=0` and
`cache_write=0`. The existing predicate never fires, so extending it would silently do nothing.

A SEPARATE helper is required, with this predicate:

    caching_requested AND usage.cache_read_tokens == 0 AND usage.cache_write_tokens == 0 AND usage.input_tokens > 0

- "caching_requested" is embodied by the existing local the runner already computes for the cache gate —
  `cache_settings is not None` (equivalently `caps.prompt_cache_style != "none"`). No new state is needed.
- It is invoked at the same seam as `_warn_if_zeroed_usage`, i.e. after `_extract_usage()` on the success path,
  and is gated on `self._model_override is None` for the same reason that guard is (test doubles report no usage).
- WARNING level, observability only, NEVER blocking — an ineffective cache is a cost problem, not a correctness
  one, and must not fail a gate run.
- The message must name the model id and both counters, so the operator can act (switch to a
  measured-caching model id) rather than merely learn that something is wrong.

### Decision C — `temperature` is FATAL on Bedrock for some models (found by measurement, not in the original plan)

`us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` with `temperature=0` returns **400 `ValidationException: temperature is
deprecated for this model`**; the identical call without it succeeds. Reproduced through pydantic-ai as well:
`BedrockConverseModel` + `BedrockModelSettings(temperature=0.0)` → `ModelHTTPError` 400.

This breaks rebar's gates on Bedrock, not just a corner case: `runner.py` sets `model_settings["temperature"]`
whenever `cfg.temperature`/`req.config.temperature` is set, and the plan-review **Pass-2 verifiers deliberately
send `temperature=0`** so re-verifying a finding does not resample. Critically,
`_drop_unsupported_sampling_settings` exists ONLY in pydantic-ai's `models/anthropic.py`, **not** in
`models/bedrock.py` — so the direct-Anthropic path degrades gracefully (warning: "Sampling parameters
['temperature'] are not supported … will be ignored") and the Bedrock path hard-fails.

**Decision: carry it as a capability — but f184's override table must first learn the MODEL NAME.**

An earlier draft of this decision said "add a rebar override entry that withdraws it for the affected Bedrock
models". That is **not implementable as f184 shipped**, and the gap is worth stating precisely: f184's
`_REBAR_OVERRIDES` predicates receive only the `ModelProfile`, and `BedrockModelProfile` carries **no per-model
identifier** (verified: no model/name attribute on the profile object). So the only predicate expressible today
is "is this Bedrock-hosted Claude", which would strip `temperature` from `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` too —
the measured-good default — destroying exactly the greedy Pass-2 determinism this decision exists to protect.

So this story adds a SEPARATE, additive table rather than changing f184's contract. f184 is **closed and its
plan-review attestation is signed**, and it defines its override predicates as `Callable[[ModelProfile], bool]`;
widening that signature would silently redefine a shipped, signed contract from a downstream leaf. The rule is
that the parent wins, so f184's `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` and its `_is_claude` predicate are left **exactly** as
shipped.

1. Add `supports_temperature: bool = True` to `ModelCapabilities`.
2. Add a **second, distinct** override table, `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES: dict[str, Mapping[str, object]]`,
   keyed on the **exact** model id, applied AFTER the profile-shaped overrides. The two tables encode genuinely
   different things and are better apart than merged: f184's keys on *capability shape* (what kind of model is
   this), this one keys on *a specific model's API defect* (this exact id rejects a parameter).
3. Keys are **exact-set membership, never prefix matching**. That is both cleaner — only model ids whose
   behaviour has actually been MEASURED get an entry, so the table never speculates — and it preserves f184's
   attested criterion that `grep -n 'startswith' src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` is empty.
4. **`capabilities_for()`'s BODY changes; its public signature does not.** An earlier draft said "no signature
   change is needed anywhere", which misleadingly implied no change at all. To be exact — the shipped body reads
   only `getattr(model_or_model_string, "profile", None)` and, for strings, `partition(":")`; it never touches
   `model_name`. The required edit, stated as control flow so nothing is left to inference:

   - the private helper becomes `_capabilities_from_profile(profile, model_id: str | None)` — a PRIVATE helper,
     so this is not the signed `_REBAR_OVERRIDES`/`capabilities_for` contract f184 attested;
   - **path 1 (model object):** `model_id = getattr(model_or_model_string, "model_name", None)` (verified: a
     `BedrockConverseModel` returns e.g. `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`), passed alongside the profile;
   - **path 2 (model string):** the id is the value `partition(":")` ALREADY produces — reuse it, do not re-parse;
   - **path 3 (conservative fallback):** no id is available, so no model-id override applies — the conservative
     record is returned unchanged, exactly as today;
   - **ordering inside the helper:** derive the fields from the profile, apply f184's profile-shaped
     `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` first (unchanged, first-match-wins), THEN apply
     `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES.get(model_id, {})` on top, so an exact-id entry wins over a shape-based one.
     A model id absent from the table changes nothing.

   `capabilities_for()`'s own parameter list, and f184's predicate signature, both stay as shipped.
5. `runner.py` omits `temperature` from `model_settings` when the capability is False, logging once at INFO that
   it did and why.

**This is model-id matching, and that is deliberate, not a relapse.** The epic's criterion forbids selecting
*provider behaviour* by matching a *provider-name* string; recording a known per-model API defect is a different
thing, and it is what pydantic-ai itself does — its profile functions dispatch on `model_name`
(`anthropic_model_profile(model_name)`), and upstream's own `anthropic_disallows_sampling_settings` flag exists
for exactly this class of quirk on the Anthropic side.

**Honest limitation: the list will drift** as AWS deprecates sampling parameters on more models, and an
unlisted-but-affected model still hard-fails. A denylist is chosen over an allowlist because an
unknown-but-affected model then fails LOUDLY, whereas an allowlist would silently drop temperature from an
unknown-but-fine model and let verdicts resample — a quiet correctness risk is worse than a loud configuration
error.

#### The drift mitigation, specified (catch site, predicate, output)

An earlier draft promised to "translate a 400 naming a sampling parameter into an actionable error" without
saying where or how, which is not implementable. Concretely:

**Catch site.** `runner.run()`'s existing `except Exception as exc` block (the one that wraps a systemic provider
failure into `LLMUnavailableError`). The translation is attempted FIRST; only if it returns `None` does the
existing `LLMUnavailableError` path run unchanged. Nothing else about that handler moves.

**Where the helper lives.** A new provider-AGNOSTIC function in the existing `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`
(already rebar's failure-classification seam):

    translate_sampling_parameter_rejection(exc, model_id: str) -> LLMConfigError | None

It must NOT live in the Bedrock leaf and must NOT introduce a provider-name branch in `runner.py` — the epic's
criterion forbids that, and any provider could in principle reject a sampling parameter. It keys on the ERROR
CONTENT, never on the provider name.

**Detection predicate**, grounded in the measured strings rather than invented. boto3 raises
`ValidationException: The model returned the following errors: 'temperature' is deprecated for this model.`;
through pydantic-ai the same failure surfaces as
`ModelHTTPError: status_code: 400, model_name: us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7, body: {'Error': {'Message': ...}}`.
So the predicate is, on the exception or its `__cause__`:

- it looks like a client request rejection — `getattr(exc, "status_code", None) == 400` OR `"ValidationException"`
  appears in `str(exc)`; AND
- `str(exc)` mentions one of the sampling parameters rebar can send — `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`; AND
- it mentions a rejection word — `deprecated`, `not supported`, or `unsupported`.

All three conjuncts are required, so an unrelated 400 (a malformed request, a bad model id) is NOT swallowed and
keeps its existing `LLMUnavailableError` classification.

**Output.** An `LLMConfigError` naming (a) the model id, (b) the offending parameter, and (c) BOTH remedies: add
the id to `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` with `supports_temperature=False`, or unset the temperature config.
The whole point is that the operator learns what to change, not merely that something failed.

Rejected alternatives: dropping temperature on ALL Bedrock calls (loses Pass-2 greedy determinism on the
measured-good default); catching the 400 and retrying without it (burns a billable, often multi-minute agentic
call and keys on model-specific error text).

Note this also widens f184's signed capability record, which story 343b stamps into the verdict sidecar — doing
it now is cheaper than after that payload shape is signed in the field. It directly de-risks story eb6e (the
production review-bot cutover with no Anthropic fallback), which would otherwise hard-fail on such a model.

**Alternative rejected:** OpenAI-compatible gateway fronting Bedrock (PR #121). No proxy is needed for the
native path, and the gateway path measurably loses caching and native structured output.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` (**new leaf**, mirroring `anthropic_model.py`) — the `bedrock` builder and
  its `BedrockProvider`/`BedrockConverseModel` construction. It does NOT go in `providers.py`: that file is at
  289 LOC against the **300-LOC cap that is an attested criterion of closed story 7468**, so the builder
  would breach a signed criterion. `providers.py` gains only the one-line registry entry.
- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — `supports_temperature` on the record plus a NEW exact-id
  `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` table (Decision C). f184's `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` predicate signature and
  `_is_claude` are left UNCHANGED — that contract is closed and signed. The profile override for Bedrock-hosted Claude and the `prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"`
  cache-settings selection are **ALREADY SHIPPED by closed story f184** — verify, do not re-add.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — omit `temperature` when the capability withdraws it, and add the Decision B
  cache-zero warning. **BLOCKED ON task `2682-b015-4fe5-4066` (the runner.py split), which MUST land first.**
  Both additions are strictly positive LOC and `runner.py` is at EXACTLY the 800-LOC hard cap, so there is no
  net-neutral way to make them: an earlier draft said "net-neutral or the split lands first" without naming
  a dependency, which left an implementer facing a signed-criterion conflict with no resolution. The split is
  now a recorded blocking edge, not an aspiration. Story `343b` (verdict provenance) needs the same headroom.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — Bedrock region + model-id/inference-profile config keys.
- `pyproject.toml` — a `[bedrock]` optional extra (`pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]`), AND that same extra added to
  the **`dev`** extra so this story's unit tests actually RUN in CI rather than skipping.

  The runtime posture is unchanged and that is the point: `[agents]` does not gain boto3, so
  `pip install nava-rebar[agents]` still has no AWS dependency (an explicit AC below). But `BedrockConverseModel`
  and `BedrockModelSettings` are unimportable without it, so without the dev entry every builder-construction
  assertion would be `importorskip`-ed away in CI and the criteria would only ever be provable on a developer's
  machine. This is the SAME precedent story `dc0d` set for `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]`, and the same one `mcp`
  already sets — an optional runtime extra that `dev` installs so its tests are real. Note most of this story's
  new logic (the `supports_temperature` override, the cache-zero warning, the 400 translation) is deliberately
  testable with profile STUBS and needs no boto3 at all; only construction does.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerated.
- `tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py` (new); `tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py` (new, env-gated).

  **It MUST live under `tests/external/`, not a new `tests/live/`.** An earlier draft said `tests/live/`,
  which does not exist and would have been a live landmine: `tests/conftest.py` (a) auto-applies the
  `external` marker to every item under `tests/external/`, and (b) HARD-FAILS collection for any item marked
  `external` that lives outside it. A canary at `tests/live/` would therefore either be collected by the
  default CI selection (`-m "not integration and not external"`) and make billable AWS calls on every CI
  run, or — if marked `external` by hand — break collection for the WHOLE suite. Existing precedents to
  follow: `tests/external/test_completion_pass_live.py`, `tests/external/test_deps_live.py`.

## Testing

Two tiers, because the mechanism spans a pure construction path and a real external service.

- Unit (construction, mocked boto3 client): the builder produces a `BedrockConverseModel` whose settings carry
  **exactly the two** `bedrock_cache_*` keys the parity decision above fixes —
  `bedrock_cache_instructions` and `bedrock_cache_tool_definitions` — and NOT `bedrock_cache_messages`; a plain on-demand id and an inference-profile ARN both construct; a missing
  `[bedrock]` extra raises `LLMConfigError` naming the install command. Contrast case: an `anthropic` model
  still gets `anthropic_cache_*`, never `bedrock_cache_*`.
- Live canary (env-gated, `REBAR_LIVE_BEDROCK=1`, skipped in default CI): issue the same cached-prefix request
  twice and assert `usage.cache_read_tokens > 0` on the second — the observable oracle for "caching works".
  Run it for both the on-demand id and the inference-profile ARN and record both results.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] `REBAR_LLM_MODEL=bedrock:<claude-id> rebar review-plan <ticket>` completes with a valid structured verdict
      against real Bedrock, output attached as a comment on this ticket
- [x] **MEASURED** — the cache canary result is recorded on this ticket: on-demand ids are not invokable at all
      here; `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` caches (`cache_write=4017` then `cache_read=4017`, reproducible);
      `us.`/`global.` opus-4-5 silently do not cache. rebar documents `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` as the
      default
- [ ] a test asserts rebar WARNS when caching was requested but both cache counters are zero (Decision B),
      since the failure is otherwise silent and bills full input every call
- [ ] a test asserts `temperature` is omitted for a model whose `supports_temperature` capability is False,
      and still sent for one where it is True (Decision C) — the contrast case
- [ ] unit tests pass with no AWS credentials present (boto3 client mocked), proving default CI is unaffected
- [ ] the live canary lives under `tests/external/` and is EXCLUDED by the default selection
      `-m "not integration and not external"` — verified by confirming the default suite's collected count is
      unchanged by its addition, so CI never makes a billable AWS call
- [ ] `pip install nava-rebar[agents]` still installs without boto3 (`python -c "import boto3"` fails in that env)
- [ ] f184's shipped contract is untouched: `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` predicates still take a single `ModelProfile`
      argument and `grep -n 'startswith' src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` is still empty
- [ ] a test asserts a provider error matching the MEASURED shape (400 / ValidationException + a sampling
      parameter name + a rejection word) becomes an `LLMConfigError` naming the model id, the parameter, and
      both remedies — and a CONTRAST case asserts an unrelated 400 still becomes `LLMUnavailableError`, so the
      translation cannot swallow unrelated failures
- [ ] `grep -n 'bedrock\|anthropic' src/rebar/llm/failure.py` shows no provider-name branch — the translation
      keys on error CONTENT only
- [ ] a test asserts the conservative-fallback path still returns the unchanged conservative record when no
      model id is available (the third path above), so adding the second table cannot alter it
- [ ] a test asserts an exact-id override WINS over a profile-shaped one for the same model (ordering)
- [ ] a test asserts the model-id override can distinguish two Bedrock model ids — `temperature` withdrawn for
      a measured-affected id and RETAINED for `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` — the contrast case that proves
      the widened predicate actually discriminates rather than blanket-stripping
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the FULL gating suite (`make test`) pass, evidenced
      by the Gerrit change id and its `Verified +1` vote recorded in a comment on this ticket (this criterion's
      proof is external to the repo, so it is attested rather than code-verifiable)
